inspiration.observed_pattern: A grouped statistics query computes a continuous percentile over ordered numeric observations alongside aggregate summaries.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reauthored as a segment report using ROW_NUMBER and COUNT windows to derive the continuous 75th-percentile interpolation because MariaDB 10.11.7 lacks native PERCENTILE_CONT. The lower and upper ordered observations are selected per segment and linearly interpolated, with singleton and exact-rank groups handled by the same formula.

fixture_notes: North has four observations, so its 75th percentile interpolates between 40 and 80 to 50. South has three observations, so it interpolates between 15 and 25 to 20. East is a singleton and remains 99.
determinism_notes: Segment and observation IDs are fixed, each value has a unique observation ID for tie-breaking, and the final report is explicitly ordered. No clocks, randomness, limits, or concurrent schedules are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE segment_observations (observation_id INT PRIMARY KEY, segment_code VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL, measurement INT NOT NULL)

steps.sql: WITH ranked AS (SELECT segment_code, measurement, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY segment_code ORDER BY measurement, observation_id) AS value_rank, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY segment_code) AS value_count FROM segment_observations), targets AS (SELECT segment_code, value_rank, measurement, value_count, 1 + 0.75 * (value_count - 1) AS target_rank FROM ranked), bounds AS (SELECT segment_code, MAX(target_rank) AS target_rank, MAX(FLOOR(target_rank)) AS lower_rank, MAX(CEIL(target_rank)) AS upper_rank, MAX(CASE WHEN value_rank = FLOOR(target_rank) THEN measurement END) AS lower_value, MAX(CASE WHEN value_rank = CEIL(target_rank) THEN measurement END) AS upper_value FROM targets GROUP BY segment_code) SELECT segment_code, CASE WHEN lower_rank = upper_rank THEN lower_value ELSE lower_value + (upper_value - lower_value) * (target_rank - lower_rank) END AS percentile_75 FROM bounds ORDER BY segment_code

checks.sql: SELECT observation_id, segment_code, measurement FROM segment_observations ORDER BY observation_id
